newsitem.title: USA: News Corp's Fox upfront ad market up.
newsitem.headline: News Corp's Fox upfront ad market up.

text.p: News Corp Ltd's Fox Broadcasting unit generated about US$1.1 billion in upfront advertising for the coming fall primetime TV season, Jon Nesvig, president of Fox's national advertising TV sales, said Wednesday.
Fox recorded about US$960 million in upfront sales last year, Nesvig said. The network's primetime ad rates rose 12-14 percent this year.

Like the other networks, Fox's biggest advertisers were automakers and movie companies, but it also drew significant chunks of ad dollars from financial services and technology companies, Nesvig said.

Nesvig estimated the network would likely sell about 85 percent of its commercial time in advance of the season's start, up from about 75 percent last year. "The economic outlook seems to be good," Nesvig said. "The scattered market has been a crapshoot for advertisers due to strong demand and ratings shortfalls, and the scattered market's been pretty expensive."

He estimated the industry upfront market totalled about $6.3 billion, including the so-called baby networks United Paramount Network, owned by Viacom Inc VIA.A and Chris-Craft Industries Inc CCN.N , and Time Warner Inc's TWX.N WB Network.
